paper_title: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Abusive Language Detection in Low-Resource   Settings
caption: : Task-wise Class Distributions
model_annotation: The provided chart, titled “Task-wise Class Distributions,” is a multi-layered radial (sunburst) visualization that illustrates the distribution of abusive and non-abusive language categories across different thematic domains for the TiALD benchmark. At the center, the dataset is split into two main branches: “Abusive” (in teal) and “Not Abusive” (in yellow). The “Abusive” branch further divides into subcategories: “Political,” “Racial,” “Sexist,” “Religious,” and “Other,” each of which is then subdivided by sentiment polarity—“Negative,” “Mixed,” and in some cases “Positive” or “Neutral.” For example, “Political” abuse is predominantly “Negative,” while “Religious” abuse includes smaller segments for “Positive,” “Mixed,” and “Neutral.” The “Not Abusive” branch similarly breaks down into “Political,” “Religious,” and “Other,” with each subdivided into “Positive,” “Neutral,” “Negative,” and “Mixed” sentiments. The “Other” category under “Not Abusive” is the largest single segment, followed by “Other” under “Abusive.” The chart uses color-coding to distinguish between abusive (teal) and non-abusive (yellow) content, with further segmentation by topic and sentiment. No explicit percentages are labeled, but relative proportions are visually represented by slice size, with the largest segments being “Other” under both abusive and non-abusive categories. The visualization effectively conveys the hierarchical structure and relative prevalence of different types of language across tasks in the benchmark.
